newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Some HIV victims may not be not be traced - minister.
newsitem.headline: Some HIV victims may not be not be traced - minister.

text.p: Ireland's health minister Michael Noonan told parliament on Tuesday that 10 patients who were given HIV-infected blood between 1981 and 1985 may never be traced.
At question time the Minister outlined the efforts of the Blood Services Transfusion Board to trace the many patients who got this infected blood, either in a transfusion or in a blood product.
Only 10 remained untraced and these may never be traced, he said.
In a bid to find them, a voluntary HIV test is being offered from January 1997 on, to anyone who got a transfusion or a blood product during that period.

The handling by the blood board of the search for patients who may have got HIV in that manner may be referred to the tribunal now dealing with the hepatitis C controversy, he said. That would only happen if he decides to amend the terms of reference of that tribunal.
Another possibility was the setting up of another tribunal to deal with the HIV issue, he said.

Minister Noonan also told the House that he would have preferred if the Blood Board had told him earlier, about this search for infected patients. The Board had told him they wanted to know the extent of the problem, before they informed him.
The Board wrote to 45 hospitals last August to try to find out who got the infected blood - but their letter did not mention that the blood was infected with HIV.
